The plan had a $450 in-network deductible, a $6,250 per-person out-of-pocket maximum, and $25 in-network office co-pays; dental is optional at extra cost. The attachment says 3,494 students received the subsidy.

summary: The university paid 88 percent of the $3,773 annual premium of the graduate student health plan in 2024-25 for graduate students with a 50 percent or greater appointment.
note: The attachment says 3,870 students received the subsidy; plan terms ($450 deductible, $6,250 out-of-pocket maximum, $25 co-pay) are the same as in 2025-26.

searched: Every mention of 'summer' in Policy 6210 (sections 2.2, 2.3, 2.3.1, 2.5 (appointment periods), 2.6, 2.7, and 6.0; PDF pages 2-6 and 9), the 2023-24 through 2026-27 stipend tables (which print 9-month and 12-month totals but say nothing on who receives a 12-month appointment), and the June 2025 and June 2026 Board compensation attachments.
summary: Neither Policy 6210 nor the stipend tables guarantee summer funding; summer assistantships exist but are not promised.
note: Policy 6210 section 2.3.1 covers summer assistantships only to say enrollment is not required and in-state tuition is not remitted in summer unless the contract says so.

summary: The Board of Visitors approved a 3.0 percent advance of the stipend scale effective August 10, 2025, raised the academic-year supplement from $458 to $565, and set the table minimum at $2,800 a month.
note: VT News reports that the Board approved the plan in June 2025, and the published 2025-26 table, effective August 10, 2025, carries the plan's $2,800 minimum. The same plan cut the scale from 50 pay ranges to 11 (Steps 1-11, plus Step 0 for fellowship combinations). Stipend rates are recorded from the published tables, not computed from this percentage.

summary: The Board approved a 2.0 percent advance of the stipend scale for 2026-27, effective August 10, 2026, subject to change with the state's employee pay program; the published 2026-27 table sets a higher minimum ($2,909 a month) than the plan proposed ($2,867).
note: The same plan proposed raising the supplement from $565 to $665 (which the published table reflects) and the table minimum to $2,867. The published 2026-27 table's Step 1 minimum is $2,909, above the proposed $2,867, so the increase applied evidently differed from the 2.0 percent proposed; no source retrieved states the final percentage. VT News reports that the Board approved the plan on June 2, 2026 (giving the minimum as $2,866), and that compensation programs would follow the final state budget, expected later that month.

Exhibit B's PhD minimum is an annual figure for both the 12-month and 9-month classifications. The twelve-month stipend comes from the GSAS funding policy, not the agreement.
summary: The agreement has no separate summer funding provision.

schools: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
summary: In most departments and programs, GSAS PhD students are guaranteed five years of twelve-month stipend support, so the stipend continues through the summer.
note: The bulletin qualifies the guarantee with 'in most departments and programs'; the GSAS funding page says full funding normally extends for at least five years. Stipends are paid semi-monthly, and Yale's Local 33 page describes the spring 2024 stipend period as January-August. First-year students' stipends are paid in 25 semi-monthly payments (twelve and a half months), while continuing students' payments start September 15. First-year PhD students are normally not appointed as Teaching Fellows (GSAS bulletin), and first-year School of Engineering and Applied Science students (other than in Computer Science) and Combined Program in Biology and Biomedical Sciences students appointed as Research Assistants are excluded from the bargaining unit (Exhibit A).

searched: Every mention of "tuition" in the agreement: PDF page 6 (management rights to establish tuition), pages 18 and 26 (waiving tuition only for required work-related training), and page 38 (Article 31, Fees, which excludes tuition). Tuition is covered by the GSAS funding policy, not the agreement.
summary: The agreement has no tuition remission or waiver provision.

schools: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
summary: Every GSAS PhD student receives a fellowship for the full cost of tuition; most departments and programs guarantee five years of tuition support.
note: The amount is the 2026-27 tuition for a year of full-time study ($26,200 per term); the bulletin anticipates tuition increases in later years.

summary: The agreement waives no fees; it bars the University from creating or charging new fees designed to offset the negotiated wage and benefit improvements.
note: Article 31 says fees do not include tuition. Elsewhere the agreement waives fees, charges, and tuition only for training the University requires.

schools: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
summary: For a standard assistantship in research (AR) appointment, the grant pays, in addition to the salary, half of the tuition or the full Continuous Registration Fee (CRF).
note: The amount is the 2026-27 Continuous Registration Fee for the year ($880 per term); GSAS's cost-of-attendance page lists it as the Continuing Registration Fee, $1,760. The bulletin says appointment to a university post does not exempt a student from registration and payment of other fees. The cost-of-attendance page adds that in some cases the Graduate School also covers the fee for advanced PhD students, without saying which.

summary: The University pays 100% of the coverage rates for Yale Health basic student health services and hospitalization/specialty care coverage for PhD graduate workers, their legal spouses, and eligible children.
note: The GSAS bulletin describes the same coverage as a Health Award for eligible PhD students, covering Student + Spouse, Student + Child(ren), and Family plans. Article 34 also covers dental insurance and lets graduate workers buy EyeMed vision insurance, with no University contribution stated.

summary: From October 1, 2024, the University offers a dental plan to PhD graduate workers and pays 80% of the single-coverage premium.
note: From the third year of enrollment, the University also pays 40% of the additional premium for single + one dependent or family coverage.

schools: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
summary: GSAS provides Yale Health Basic Coverage at no cost to master's and PhD students enrolled at least half-time in degree programs.
note: Basic Coverage does not include hospitalization/specialty care; only PhD students receive the Health Fellowship Award for that. Master's students in the Local 33 unit have no health provision in the agreement, whose Article 34 covers PhD students only. The GSAS pages do not describe professional-school students' coverage.

schools: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
summary: All GSAS PhD students registered at least half-time receive a Health Fellowship Award that covers the cost of Yale Health Hospitalization/Specialty Care Coverage.
note: The amount is the 2026-27 twelve-month rate for a single student; dependent coverage costs more, and the Local 33 agreement (Article 34) has the University pay 100% of the rates for the PhD worker's spouse and children too. GSAS's cost-of-attendance page says packages cover half the cost of two-person coverage; the agreement and the GSAS bulletin say the full cost.
